problem: E14 executed a real self-improvement once -- it was not yet known whether that result was a one-time success or a reproducible mechanism that holds as real data grows.

decision.decision_summary: Replayed E14's exact functions against the same real data (byte-identical reproduction check), then re-applied them to the real, grown data set (E1..E14) to check consistency, then re-ran the 3 regression conditions and full safety checks. No new execution performed.

action.action_summary: Reused currencyGuard (E11), prioritizeCandidate (E13), computeGoalTrackRecord + applyTrackRecordTieBreaker (E14) verbatim; added no new weight or signal.

result.note: Verifies PB's own improvement mechanism; does not change this Goal's own real status. No code executed, no candidate applied.

cause.root_cause_summary: A single successful self-improvement execution (E14) does not by itself prove the mechanism is reproducible or that it will keep behaving consistently as real data grows -- that required a dedicated verification pass.

lesson: E14's tie-breaker reproduces deterministically on the same data, and remains internally consistent on grown real data without any new weighting -- and this verification pass itself surfaced a genuine, previously-undocumented structural fact (an intra-goal_ref tie can never be broken by a goal-scoped track record, since both sides always move together), which is more useful than a verification that had found nothing.
